a11y.name: Its heading.

anatomy.content: rows or details, the 12 px inset at the sides

anatomy.surface: the card fill, radius 24 at the top corners, a hairline, elevation 2

components.name: Bottom sheet

rules.text: A bottom sheet is for narrow windows and touch; wide windows use a sheet from the toolbar or a side sheet.
A bottom sheet closes with Escape and shows its grab handle.

components.summary: A sheet anchored to the bottom edge of a narrow window or a touch surface, with a grab handle on top.

a11y.name: Each link by its page title.

anatomy.crumb: a plain button in the accent ink, 24 tall, 4 px each side
anatomy.current: body text, medium, ellipsized in the middle when long
anatomy.separator: a 16 px chevron in the dim ink

copy.crumb: The page titles exactly as their pages say them.

keyboard.Tab: Moves through the parent links.

components.name: Breadcrumb

rules.text: The last crumb is the current page and is not a link.
Do not use a breadcrumb for a flat set of pages; use the sidebar or tabs.

states.deep: Three parents and a long current page.
states.two: One parent and the current page.

components.summary: Shows where a page sits in a hierarchy; each parent is a link back, the current page is plain text at the end.

a11y.name: The group by what its buttons do (Text Style); every button by its label or tooltip.

anatomy.block: 24 tall, radius 8 on the outer corners only, the control fill
anatomy.item: a glyph or one word; the same height as a button

keyboard.Tab: Moves through the buttons one by one.

components.name: Button group

rules.text: A button group has two to five buttons; for exactly one choice from several use the segmented control.
A button group is named for assistive technology, and every glyph button in it has a tooltip.

states.glyphs: Three glyph buttons (Zoom Out, Zoom In, Full Screen).

components.summary: Buttons that belong together, joined into one block: Zoom Out, Zoom In, Full Screen. Each acts alone.

a11y.name: Its title, when it has one.

anatomy.outlined: the card fill and a hairline
anatomy.surface: radius 12, the inset on all four sides (12; compact 8, comfortable 16)

copy.title: Title Case for the card title, sentence case for its text.

keyboard.Tab: Moves to the controls inside the card; the card itself takes no focus unless it is one button.

components.name: Card

rules.text: A card insets its content equally on all four sides by the density's inset.
Use one card style per surface: elevated on the window ground, filled inside another card, outlined in dense lists.
Do not nest an elevated card in an elevated card.

components.summary: Holds one subject (an app, a photo, a summary) on a surface of its own: elevated, filled or outlined.

a11y.name: The step buttons by their names (Previous, Next).

anatomy.steps: previous and next icon buttons on a card disc with elevation 1
anatomy.strip: items 8 px apart, scrolling sideways with no scrollbar

keyboard.Tab: Moves to the previous button, the items, then the next button.

components.name: Carousel

rules.text: A carousel can be moved with its buttons and the keyboard, never only by dragging.
Do not advance a carousel by itself.

states.start: At the start, more items to the right.

components.summary: A row of items that scrolls sideways (featured apps, photos) with previous and next buttons at its ends.

a11y.description: The row subtitle, when the box sits in a row.
a11y.name: Its own label.

anatomy.box: 16 px square, radius 4, a hairline of the text at 36 percent; card fill
anatomy.check: the accent fill with the check mark in the accent ink (or a dash when mixed)
anatomy.label: body text 13/20, 8 px after the box

copy.label: Sentence case, a noun phrase or a short clause that is true when the box is on: Show hidden files.

keyboard.Tab: Moves the focus to the box.

components.name: Checkbox

rules.text: Use a checkbox for an option among several that can be on together; for one setting that applies at once use a switch.
A checkbox carries its label and the label toggles it too.
Do not phrase a checkbox label as a negative (Do not show); say what is true when it is on.

states.disabled: The option cannot change now; the text near it says why.
states.mixed: Some of the options the box stands for are on; a click turns them all on.

components.summary: Turns one option of a list on or off, where several can be on at once and nothing applies until the list is used.

a11y.name: Its label; a filter chip is a toggle button with the pressed state; the remove button by its tooltip.

anatomy.glyph: 16 px, assist only, in the accent ink; a filter chip that is on shows a check
anatomy.label: 13 medium, one to three words

keyboard.Enter: Activates the chip or flips the filter.
keyboard.Space: Activates the chip or flips the filter.
keyboard.Tab: Moves the focus to the chip (and to its remove button).

components.name: Chip

rules.text: Chips appear in a set, 8 px apart, about the content above or below them; never as the main action of a surface.
A filter chip shows a check when it is on, so the state is not colour alone.
An input chip's remove button is named Remove followed by what it removes.
Do not put more than eight chips in a set; use a dropdown or a search field.

states.assist: An assist chip with its glyph (Add to Calendar).
states.filter-on: A filter that is on: the accent tint and a check.
states.input: Something the person entered, with its remove button.

components.summary: A compact element that starts a related action, filters a view, stands for something entered, or offers a suggestion.

a11y.name: The field by what the date is for (Start Date); the button by Choose Date.

anatomy.button: an icon button with the calendar glyph, 8 px from the field

anatomy.invalid: a 1 px danger ring on the field and the field marked invalid for assistive technology

copy.label: What the date is for, in Title Case: Start Date.

keyboard.Tab: Moves from the field to the calendar button.

components.name: Date input

rules.text: A date field says the shape it wants and marks a day that does not exist as invalid for assistive technology, not by colour alone.
A date field always comes with the calendar button, so a far date is a click away.

states.invalid: Ten characters typed that are not a real day (2026-02-30).

components.summary: A date typed in a field in the shape YYYY-MM-DD, with the calendar button beside it.

a11y.name: The month and year; every day by its full date (Monday 26 October 2026).

anatomy.card: the card fill, a hairline, radius 12, the 12 px inset
anatomy.day: 28 px circle; today a 1 px accent ring; the picked day the accent disc
anatomy.header: month and year (13 semibold), previous and next buttons at the end
anatomy.weekdays: the letters M T W T F S S in the dim caption, weeks from Monday

copy.month: Full month name and the year: October 2026.

keyboard.Tab: Moves through the month buttons and into the days.

components.name: Date picker

rules.text: Every day button is named by its full date for assistive technology, not by its number alone.
Weeks start on Monday, like the calendar widget.
Do not make a person scroll month by month to a far date; offer a text field for typing it as well.

components.summary: Picks one day from a month grid, with the previous and next month a click away and today marked.

a11y.name: The month and year; every day by its full date (Monday 26 October 2026).

anatomy.card: the card fill, a hairline, radius 12, the 12 px inset

anatomy.header: month and year (13 semibold), previous and next buttons at the end
anatomy.weekdays: the letters M T W T F S S in the dim caption, weeks from Monday

copy.month: Full month name and the year: October 2026.

keyboard.Space: Picks the focused day as the first, then the last day.
keyboard.Tab: Moves through the month buttons and into the days.

components.name: Date range picker

rules.text: Every day button is named by its full date for assistive technology, not by its number alone.
A range picker starts a new range at the third click and never keeps a half range once the second end is picked.

states.picked: A range is picked: the two ends in the accent, the days between tinted.

components.summary: Picks a first and a last day from a month grid; the days between are tinted.

a11y.name: The header title.

anatomy.body: the hidden part, under the header
anatomy.header: a row of the list-row height: chevron in the dim ink, 8 px, then the title 13 medium

components.name: Disclosure

rules.text: A disclosure exposes its expanded state, so a screen reader says open or closed.
Do not hide something a person needs on most visits behind a disclosure.

components.summary: A header that shows and hides the part under it (advanced options, details), with a chevron that turns.

a11y.description: The value in words when the number alone is unclear (Level 3 of 5).

components.name: Discrete slider

rules.text: A discrete slider has three to eleven stops; more is a continuous slider.
The value of a discrete slider always sits on a stop; a drag between stops snaps.

components.summary: Picks a value that only makes sense in whole steps (a level from 1 to 5), with a tick at each stop.

a11y.name: None.

anatomy.line: 1 px of the line colour; inset 12 px at both ends when inset

components.hig: hig.md section 2 (hairline inset, never to the frame edge)

a11y.name: Its label, or its tooltip when it shows a glyph alone.

copy.label: A verb phrase in Title Case: New Note.

components.hig: hig.md section 1 (one primary action per surface)

components.name: Floating action button

A floating action button with a glyph alone has a tooltip, which is its name.

components.summary: The one main action of a touch or narrow surface that has no toolbar for it; a glyph alone or extended with words.

a11y.name: The toolbar by what it acts on (Image Tools); every action by its tooltip.

anatomy.action: a 24 px icon button, a circle on hover
anatomy.pill: 32 tall, a pill, the glass fill, elevation 3, a hairline

states.primary: Two icon buttons and a primary one at the end.

components.summary: A pill that floats over content with the few actions of that content, such as undo, redo and copy in an image editor.

a11y.name: The trailing control is labelled by the title and described by the supporting text.

anatomy.leading: nothing, a 16 px glyph, a 32 px avatar or a 32 px picture, 12 px before the text
anatomy.supporting: secondary 11/16; wraps; a three-line item shows two lines and ellipsizes
anatomy.title: body 13/20
anatomy.trailing: a control or a short text at the end, named by the title

components.hig: hig.md section 1 (rows); the row height is the list-row spec's

keyboard.Tab: Moves to the trailing control, when there is one.

components.name: List item

rules.text: A trailing control in a list item is named by the item's title.
A three-line item ellipsizes its supporting text after two lines instead of growing.
Do not mix one-, two- and three-line items in one list without a reason a person can see.

states.avatar: A person: an avatar, a name and an address.
states.three-line: Title and two supporting lines with a picture.
states.trailing: A trailing switch named by the title.

components.summary: The content layouts of a list row: one, two or three lines, with a leading glyph, avatar or picture and a trailing control.

a11y.name: Each item by its label.

anatomy.item: a flat button, the label 13 and the shortcut dim at the end, 24 px gap

keyboard.Letters: Move to the next item that starts with them.

rules.text: A menu item says what it does in Title Case and shows its shortcut at the end in the dim ink.
A context menu offers the same verbs as the toolbar, with the same names and keys.
Do not put more than twelve items in a menu without separators between groups.

components.summary: A short list of commands that opens from a button or a right-click, each a verb, with its shortcut at the end.

a11y.name: Each destination by its label.

anatomy.bar: glass fill with a hairline on top, 52 tall
anatomy.destination: a 16 px glyph in a 24 x 48 pill over an 11 px label; equal shares of the width
anatomy.picked: the pill takes the accent at 18 percent and the glyph the accent ink

components.name: Navigation bar

rules.text: A navigation bar shows only when the window is narrower than 640 px; wider windows use the sidebar.
Every destination has a glyph and a label; never a glyph alone.

components.summary: Three to five destinations at the bottom of a narrow window, in place of the sidebar.

a11y.name: The drawer by its title; each destination by its label.

keyboard.Tab: Moves to the picked destination.

components.name: Navigation drawer

Every drawer destination has a glyph and a label, and the drawer is named by its title.

a11y.name: Each destination by its label.

anatomy.picked: the pill in the accent at 18 percent
anatomy.rail: 84 wide, the sidebar fill, a hairline at the end

copy.label: One word in Title Case per destination.

keyboard.Tab: Moves to the picked destination.

components.name: Navigation rail

rules.text: A rail replaces the sidebar between the narrow breakpoint and the sidebar's width; never both at once.
Every rail destination has a glyph and a label.

components.summary: Three to seven destinations in a narrow column at the start of a window too narrow for the sidebar.

a11y.name: The level's name (Volume).

anatomy.pill: glass, radius 999, the same 8 px inside on all four sides, at least 216 wide

components.name: On-screen display

rules.text: The on-screen display never takes the keyboard from the app in front.
The level is a bar and a glyph, never colour alone.

Do not use a radio group to start actions; each option is a state.

states.disabled: No option can be picked now.

components.summary: Picks exactly one of two to six options that are shown at once, each with a dot.

keyboard.Tab: Moves to the low knob, then the high knob.

components.name: Range slider

rules.text: Each knob of a range slider is a slider of its own with its own name.
The low knob never passes the high knob.

states.wide: The range covers most of the track.

anatomy.surface: glass, radius 12, the 12 px inset, elevation 2

states.action: A title, a sentence and a Learn More action.

components.summary: A tooltip with a title, one or two sentences and at most one text action, which stays while the pointer is over it.

components.summary: The search field with what it found under it as rows, or one quiet line when nothing matches.

anatomy.action: a plain button at the end

states.action: A title and a See All action.

components.summary: The heading over a group of rows or cards, with at most one text action at the end (See All).

anatomy.buttons: at the end, 8 px apart, the default one last; destructive in the destructive style

states.destructive: A destructive question: Cancel and a destructive action.

Each tab panel is labelled by its tab and each tab controls its panel for assistive technology.
Do not nest primary tabs; inside a tab use secondary tabs or a segmented control.

states.scrollable: Eight tabs in a scroller narrower than them.
states.secondary: Secondary tabs inside a pane, the first picked.

components.summary: Switches between views of the same subject at one level; primary tabs change the whole pane, secondary tabs a part of it.

a11y.description: The hint or the error line under it.
a11y.name: The row title or the field label (labelled-by).

anatomy.field: the control fill, a hairline, radius 8, 8 px inside

copy.placeholder: An example of what goes in, not the label: A few words about this app.

keyboard.Tab: Moves the focus into the area (Tab inside it moves on; Ctrl+Tab types a tab).

components.name: Text area

rules.text: A text area is at least three lines (84 px) tall and grows to the content up to its page.
Do not use a text area for one line; use a text field.

states.disabled: The text can be read and not changed.

components.summary: Takes text of several lines (a note, a description) that wraps at the field's width and scrolls when long.

a11y.name: Hour and Minute.

anatomy.hour: a spin button of two digits, tabular figures
anatomy.minute: a spin button of two digits that wraps from 59 to 00

copy.names: Hour and Minute, never H and M.

keyboard.Tab: Moves from the hour to the minute.
keyboard.Up and Down: Change the focused part by one.

components.name: Time picker

rules.text: Times show two digits on each side of the colon (09:05).
The hour and the minute are named for assistive technology.

components.summary: Picks an hour and a minute on the 24-hour clock, each a two-digit field that wraps around.

a11y.description: The expanded state of a row with children.
a11y.name: Each row by its label.

anatomy.chevron: 16 px in the dim ink, turns when open

keyboard.Left: Closes it, then moves to its parent.
keyboard.Right: Opens the focused row, then moves into it.

components.name: Tree

rules.text: Right and Left open and close the focused row of a tree.
A tree row is 28 px at standard density and follows the density.

components.summary: Rows that open and close to show their children (folders, groups), with a chevron and an indent per level.
